Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

stop squabbling! phrase

also stop bickering, stop arguing

classical

Cic. de Or. 2.240: cum esset cum eō dē amiculā rīxātus (Lewis & Short s.v. rīxor)
Hor. Ep. 1.18.15: dē lānā caprīnā (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 36

Dēsinite rīxārī.

stop bickering (to several)

Rīxor: to quarrel, wrangle (Lewis & Short: rare but classical).

Other words

  • Dēsine rīxārī. — to one

    also used · classical · Traupman 34

    rīxor is classical.

  • Dēsine altercārī. — stop arguing (with words)

    also used · classical · Caes. BC 3.19: altercārī cum … incipit (Lewis & Short s.v. altercor); Liv. 3.68: mulierum rītū inter nōs altercantēs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 273

    Altercor is to dispute, have words with someone (cum aliquō, inter sē); lītigāre is to quarrel, dispute (quā dē rē lītigātis inter vōs?, Plaut. Rud. 4.4.16, Lewis & Short).

  • Dēsine argūmentārī! — said for “stop arguing!”

    avoid · modern · Traupman 93

    Argūmentor is to reason, to bring proofs (Lewis & Short), not to quarrel; for bickering say rīxārī or jūrgāre.

Examples

  • Vōs ambō, dēsinite rīxārī!

    You two, stop squabbling!composed

See also stop it!, stop talking, argument.
